Under the The doctrine of privity of contract is a common law principle which provides that a contract can not confer rights or impose obligations upon anyone who is not a party to that contract. [ 1 ] It is related to, but distinct from, the doctrine of consideration, according to which a promise is legally enforceable only if valid consideration has been provided for it, and a plaintiff is legally entitled to enforce such a promise only if he is a promisee from whom the consideration has moved. [ 2 ] A principal consequence of the doctrine of privity is that, at common law, a third party generally has no right to enforce a contract to which he is not a party, even where that contract was entered into by the contracting parties specifically for his benefit and with a common intention among all of them that he should be able to enforce it. In XXXX & XXXX and XXXX XXXX, the doctrine has been substantially weakened by the Contracts ( Rights of Third Parties ) Act 1999, which created a statutory exception to privity, providing, in certain circumstances, third parties the right to enforce terms of contracts to which they are not privy.

Consumer complaint narrative:
According to the law in 15 U.S.C 1681, consumer reporting agencies must adopt fair procedures for credit and info accuracy. But Equifax, you're not meeting my needs or being fair by reporting errors. 

Under 15 U.S.C 1681a ( d ), a consumer report covers any info from a reporting agency about a person 's credit worthiness. You can't claim to verify accounts unless you can prove it, as per 15 U.S.C 1681a ( e ), which defines an " investigative consumer report. '' There shouldn't be specific factual info about my credit record directly from a creditor, as the term " creditor '' means someone who regularly gives credit. This is a violation of 15 U.S.C 1692b ( 2 ) and 15 U.S.C 1692a ( 2 ). 

As per 15 U.S.C 1692c ( b ), communication shouldn't happen unless it involves the consumer, attorney, or a CRA if permitted by law. Only specific actions are allowed for refusal to pay a debt. 

Debt collectors aren't allowed to use any conduct that harasses, oppresses, or abuses a person in collecting a debt, as stated in 15 U.S.C 1692d. Threats or harming someone's reputation or property are also not allowed, as per 15 U.S.C 1692d ( 1 ). 

False representation about the debt or communicating false credit info is against the law, according to 15 U.S.C 1692e ( 2 ). Also, foreclosures, repossessions, wage garnishments, or arrests for debts are illegal under 15 U.S.C 1692e ( 4 ). 

If a dispute is made in writing, debt reporting must stop until the dispute is resolved, per 15 U.S.C 1692g ( b ).

According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), negative information such as a charge-off should only be reported once, corresponding to the date it was charged off. 
The FCRA requires that credit reporting agencies ensure the accuracy of the information they report ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ). Repeatedly reporting the charge-off each month results in a misleading and inaccurate credit report, which has significantly harmed my credit score.

Additionally, the statute of limitations for reporting a charge-off is seven years from the date of the first delinquency that led to the charge-off ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) ( 4 ) ). Continuously reporting this charge-off as a new event each month does not reset the statute of limitations and is improper. 
I request that you promptly investigate this account and correct the inaccurate information by removing the repeated entries of the charge-off from my payment history. Please update my credit report accordingly and provide me with a confirmation of these corrections. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter
